turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Good morning Dana, good morning Marcus. Thanks for making the time today.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Morning. Can you hear me okay?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Loud and clear. Can you hear me alright on your side?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Yes, perfectly. The line is much better than last week.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Good. I know you were travelling on Monday, how was the trip back from Manchester?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Long, honestly. The train was delayed by an hour and then it rained the whole way home.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: That sounds exhausting. I hope the weekend made up for it.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It did. We went to my sister's place and I did absolutely nothing, which was the plan.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: That is the best kind of weekend. We had a bit of monsoon here in Bengaluru, so the traffic was a nightmare as usual.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I can imagine. Marcus is just dialling in from the other office, he says hello.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Hello Marcus. Lovely to have you both. Let me share my screen so we have the agenda in front of us.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Can you see my screen? No, sorry, that is the wrong way round. Can you see yours, I mean.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: I can see mine, and I am sharing it now. Can you see my screen?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Yes, it is up. The text is a good size.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Great. The agenda has four items. First, what you are trying to fix. Second, how we have done this before. Third, how a project would work. Fourth, next steps.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: That works for us. Shall we take ten minutes at the end for next steps?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Yes, absolutely, I will keep ten minutes at the end for that.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: So, as Dana mentioned in the invite, our associates spend far too long on first pass review of contracts. We receive about four hundred N D A s a quarter, and every one is read by hand.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Four hundred a quarter is a serious backlog. And what matters most to you in fixing it?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Speed matters, of course, but Marcus is firm that nothing may leave iManage. No copies in outside storage, ever.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Understood, everything stays inside iManage. Let me note that down. Let me also tell you what we propose to do, then I will take your questions as we go.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: We would build a review assistant inside your document system. It reads an incoming agreement, proposes tracked changes against your own playbook, and every suggestion shows the playbook clause behind it. Your people accept or reject each change.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: That is roughly what we had in mind. Before we go further, let me ask about the team.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: What does a senior engineer cost per month, offshore?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: A senior engineer working offshore from Bengaluru is five thousand two hundred dollars a month. The onsite rate is higher, but most of the team would be offshore.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Okay. That is about what we expected.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: How quickly could you have a team working on this?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: A pod of up to six people can start within two weeks of signing. If you needed twenty people, that takes four weeks. If we agree in time, we could begin on the fifteenth of November.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: The fifteenth of November would suit us. We close our budget cycle just before that.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Who owns the code you write for us?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Before that, one thing on iManage, because I think it decides the architecture. We would run the whole assistant inside your iManage environment, so no document is copied anywhere outside it. Is that how Marcus pictures it?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Yes, that is exactly the picture. Nothing outside iManage.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Good, then we are aligned on that.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: If something breaks at night, how fast do you respond?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: We run a support rota that covers your hours, so a serious fault at night reaches a person quickly and not a queue. I will send the full support terms in writing after the call.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: That is fine, as long as it is written down.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: It will be. Let me move on to the work we have done in your field.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Have you automated redline review for a law firm before?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Yes. For a mid size law firm we built a redline assistant that proposes tracked changes against the firm's playbook. First pass review went from about three hours to forty minutes per agreement, and most of the proposed changes were accepted without edits.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: That is encouraging. Our partners are cautious about anything that sounds like a black box.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: We also learned a lesson there. We split the playbook into one entry per clause position before the pilot started, which saved weeks of work on matching.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Our playbook is a single long document, so that is useful to know. Marcus can tell you how it is organised.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: How do you stop the model inventing clauses in a contract?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: You keep the model tied to the text in front of it, make it point to the exact clause it used for every suggestion, and have a person accept or reject every change. If it cannot point to a clause, it should say so instead of guessing.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Good. That is the answer the partners want to hear.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Is it all right if I send you our playbook after this call?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Please do. I will keep it inside the secure folder we agreed.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Would you cap liability at twelve months of fees?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: That is one for the contract discussion. We are open to a cap, and our lawyers will want to see your draft before we agree anything.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Fair enough. We will send our draft with the playbook.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Ballpark, what would the whole project cost us?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: I would rather not guess. We would scope that properly in a paid discovery phase, and then give you a fixed price you can hold us to.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: That is reasonable. Dana will want to see the discovery plan.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Good. Let me use the last minutes for next steps. I will send the support terms and a discovery plan, you send the playbook and your draft contract, and we meet again next week.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Does Thursday work for the follow up?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Thursday works. I will send the invite today.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Thank you both. This was a useful call.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Thank you, Dana. Thank you, Marcus. Speak on Thursday.
